scope: Manual review of all 10 remaining paper-local interfaces of aos-2024-v52-i05-p2241, including the frozen source notes on SHINE splits, reciprocal likelihood ratios and nested total-variation closures; existing completed interfaces preserved.

rows.query: Pivotal statistic with common distribution across a null family; searched pivotal and inspected IdentDistrib fields and pushforward laws.
rows.result: IdentDistrib X X P P' asserts equality of the statistic's laws under two measures, with almost-everywhere measurability. Quantification over all pairs of null laws gives the source's family property.
rows.gap: The existing identical-distribution predicate suffices after quantifying it over the null family for the same measurable statistic.

comparisons.D1: Require equality of the full pushforward law for every P,P' in the null family, not merely equal expectations; exact e-variables only have null expectation one and do not acquire pivotality from exactness alone.

rows.query: SHINE recursive split-at-barycenter construction, subprobability children and weighted atomic measures; searched SHINE and inspected point masses, measure sums and vector integrals.
rows.result: Vector integration divided by mass expresses a nonzero finite measure's barycenter, and weighted point masses express each finite output law. These primitives do not choose the separating split, prove its uniqueness or provide conventions for zero-mass children.
rows.gap: SHINE still requires the recursive separating splits, their admissible choices and mass-preservation proofs, with the source's zero-mass and scalar/vector ambiguities retained.

comparisons.D20: Start with delta at the all-ones vector and root measure gamma, split every node into two diagonal-barycenter children and place each child's total mass at its barycenter; preserve the binary indices and 2^s nodes, and do not use totalized division to invent a barycenter for an empty child or infer uniqueness without the source's N condition.

rows.query: SHINE scalar first-coordinate coupling, binary-tree transition kernels, nonnegative martingale and almost-sure convergence; searched SHINE and inspected trajectory measure, Martingale and the L1-bounded submartingale convergence theorem.
rows.result: History-dependent Markov kernels can realize the split-tree law, and the martingale definition expresses its conditional barycenter equality. Once integrability, nonnegativity and constant expectation are proved, the L1 bound yields almost-everywhere convergence; pushing the limit through x -> (x,...,x) gives the diagonal limit law.
rows.gap: The SHINE coupling still needs normalized transitions and a martingale proof, including treatment of zero-mass states and any coinciding scalar node values, before the existing convergence theorem applies.

comparisons.D21: Retain X_0=1 and child-mass/parent-mass transition probabilities along the binary split tree, with the scalar first-coordinate barycenter identity; conditioning on scalar X_s values must be reconciled with node labels if values coincide, null-parent transitions are unspecified, and this coordinate corresponds to dF/dG rather than the reciprocal e-variable, so its e-power uses minus log and the limit law is that of X_infinity times the all-ones vector.

rows.query: One common dominating probability measure for null and alternative families; inspected ProbabilityMeasure and the null-set definition of AbsolutelyContinuous.
rows.result: Existential quantification over a probability measure R and absolute continuity of every law in both families directly expresses common domination.
rows.gap: These declarations suffice to state common probability domination with one shared reference measure.

comparisons.D22: Use one R with P<<R for every null P and Q<<R for every alternative Q, retaining that R is a probability measure; this is distinct from the earlier simple-alternative AC requirement P_i<<Q and implies neither mutual absolute continuity nor pivotality.

rows.query: E-power as expected log and maximization over pivotal exact e-variables; searched pivotal and inspected log, Bochner/nonnegative integration, common laws and IsMaxOn.
rows.result: On an integrable positive-log domain the objective is a Bochner integral, and IsMaxOn expresses a candidate's objective comparison once feasibility is separately required. Extended log expectations need explicit positive/negative-part conventions; Real.log 0 and nonintegrable Bochner integrals have totalized values that do not settle the source's domains.
rows.gap: The e-power optimization still needs its pivotal exact feasible set and logarithm/infinite-expectation conventions specified, with attainment proved separately.

comparisons.D14: For fixed finite null family and simple alternative Q, maximize E_Q[log X] over pivotal exact e-variables, retaining both equality of null means and equality of full null laws; do not replace log power by E_Q[X], remove pivotality, or treat IsMaxOn alone as feasibility or existence of an optimizer.

rows.query: Likelihood-ratio-law e-power optimization, diagonal density pushforward and convex-order constraint; searched convex order and inspected rnDeriv, pushforward, ConvexOn, integration, log and maximum predicates.
rows.result: The density and pushforward operations form the two vector laws, while convex test functions and integrals provide ingredients for their convex-order comparison. No complete convex-order-constrained e-power optimizer was located; extended density and log domains need explicit treatment.
rows.gap: The transformed optimization still needs the convex-order feasible law construction and objective conventions, together with the claimed equivalence to pivotal exact e-power maximization.

comparisons.D18: Retain F,G probability laws on R, objective E_G[-log(dF/dG)], the G-law of the repeated L-coordinate dF/dG vector below the Q-law of (dP_1/dQ,...,dP_L/dQ) in convex order, and the minus-log ratio direction; the derivative describes the absolutely continuous part unless the required domination is supplied, and AC of the nulls with respect to Q does not silently establish equivalence of F and G or all zero-density conventions.

rows.query: IID repeated experiment with a family of pure product laws; inspected finite product measure, mutual independence and identical distributions.
rows.result: For each fixed population law P, a finite product with every coordinate measure equal to P gives its n-observation experiment. Taking the image of the original family under this construction preserves the pure-product restriction.
rows.gap: The product experiments are composable from these declarations, while existence and power of the desired e-variable remain separate statistical claims.

comparisons.D19: Build exactly {P_1^n,...,P_L^n} and {Q^n}, using one population distribution for all n iid coordinates and an e-variable on their joint data; neither mixed-coordinate products nor products of convex mixtures belong automatically, and the product-span theorem does not inherit JA or e-variable premises from this motivation.

rows.query: Simultaneous transport of a finite tuple of measures by one stochastic kernel or map; searched simultaneous transport and inspected Kernel, Markov normalization, measure bind and deterministic pushforwards.
rows.result: A single Markov kernel and coordinatewise bind equalities express the transport plans; a single measurable map with coordinatewise pushforward equalities expresses the maps. Equal input/output masses are the source's stated compatibility condition, not a construction of such a kernel.
rows.gap: These declarations suffice to define the simultaneous feasible sets by imposing all coordinate transport equations on one shared kernel or measurable map.

comparisons.D10: For the d finite positive coordinate measures on the two Polish spaces, impose bind(mu_i,kappa)=nu_i for every i with the same stochastic kappa, or map T mu_i=nu_i for every i with the same measurable T; separate coordinate-specific kernels or maps would weaken the defining simultaneous requirement.

rows.query: Total-variation closed span and convex hull, outer closure of their sum, tight alternatives and uniform positive log e-power; inspected signed total variation, span, convexHull, tight families and log integration.
rows.result: Signed-measure total variation supplies the strong distance after applying it to a difference, and algebraic span/hull plus topological closure express the separation sets in that topology. Tightness is a uniform family property. These ingredients do not prove the source's equivalence to existence of a bounded exact e-variable with a positive infimum of log power.
rows.gap: The remaining content is the uniform e-power separation equivalence in the total-variation topology and its additional tight-family equivalence, with every printed closure preserved.

comparisons.D23: Keep 0 outside the outer closure of the sum of the individually closed span(P) and convex hull(Q); only the tight-Q clause switches to disjointness of those two closed sets, and the criterion requires inf_Q E_Q[log X]>0 for a bounded exact e-variable without pivotality; a half-versus-full variation normalization leaves closure topology unchanged, but weak probability-measure topology or pointwise positive power cannot replace the printed uniform condition.

rows.query: Usual setwise measure order on Borel sets; inspected the Measure partial-order instance and le_iff measurable-set characterization.
rows.result: With the Borel measurable-space structure, le_iff is exactly the equivalence between the standard measure order and comparison on every Borel set.
rows.gap: The existing measure order and its measurable-set characterization directly supply this definition on the Borel space.

comparisons.D6: Use ordinary positive-measure order mu<=nu iff mu(A)<=nu(A) for every Borel A, including the subprobability split measures; this compares set masses and is distinct from the convex-test-function order used elsewhere in the paper.
